topicName: Mitigating Injection Attacks in Workflow Expressions
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mitigating Injection Attacks in Workflow Expressions within GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Threat"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"GitHub Actions workflows often process untrusted input, such as pull request titles, branch names, or issue comments. When these variables are directly interpolated into workflow commands using expression syntax like ${{
 github.event.issue.title }}, they can lead to script injection vulnerabilities. Attackers can manipulate these inputs to execute arbitrary shell commands on the runner."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"The Vulnerable Pattern"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"Consider the following insecure workflow snippet that directly passes an issue title into a run command:"},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"name: Vulnerable Workflow
on: [issue_comment]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Insecure Command
        run: echo "Processing issue: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}""},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"If an attacker sets an issue title to a crafted payload like '" & malicious_command & "', the runner will interpret it as part of the shell script, leading to remote code execution."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Mitigation Strategy: Using Intermediate Environment Variables"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The recommended approach to prevent command injection is to pass untrusted data through intermediate environment variables. When you assign expression values to environment variables, GitHub Actions safely passes them to the underlying shell via argument vectors rather than direct string interpolation."},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Secure Implementation Example"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"name: Secure Workflow
on: [issue_comment]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Secure Command
        env:
          ISSUE_TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: |
          echo "Processing issue: $ISSUE_TITLE""},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Security Takeaways"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Never use direct string interpolation for untrusted contexts (github.event.*) inside run blocks."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always leverage the env context to safely isolate untrusted input."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reference the environment variables using standard shell syntax (e.g., $VARIABLE) instead of expression syntax (${
 ... }) inside execution steps."}]
